31. 2. 40

26-7-40 P.M

National Herald and Shen Pao :-

CHINESE NATURALIZATION ACQUIRED BY RUSSIAN COUPLE
IN SHANGHAI.

Mr. Oshakovsky (?) aged 63, a Russian resident in
Shanghai, and Mrs. Oshakovsky, his wife, aged 60, a Pole,
have been living in China for about nine years.
Mr. and Mrs. Oshakovsky applied to the Chungking
Government in February 1940 for naturalization as
Chinese citizens. When approved, the fellow citizenship
paper bearing the characters, "Chungking Citizen", No. 26,
was issued by post at the beginning of this month and
received by Mr. Oshakovsky on July 24.
Mr. Oshakovsky is residing at 2 Route Delastre and
is engaged in an industrial enterprise.

3e/7.

《国民公报》及《申报》：

俄籍夫妇在上海取得中国国籍

奥沙科夫斯基（Oshakovsky，音译）先生，63岁，系居住于上海的俄国人；其妻奥沙科夫斯基夫人，60岁，系波兰人。二人已在中国居住约九年。
奥沙科夫斯基夫妇于1940年2月向重庆政府申请归化为中国公民。获批后，印有“重庆市民”字样的第26号同胞证于本月初通过邮寄发出，并由奥沙科夫斯基先生于7月24日收到。
奥沙科夫斯基先生现居于德拉司特路（Route Delastre）2号，从事工业企业经营。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

REPORT

File No. MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY
S. 2. S. D. 7092
Date December 12, 1935 12/12 35

Subject Communication from the Netherlands Consulate General re
Isak Boris Katz.

Made by D.S. Tcheremshansky Forwarded by **〔此处转录不清〕**

With reference to the attached communication
enquiries show that Isak Boris Katz is a Russian of Jewish
origin, born on July 8, 1889 at Kiev, South Russia. He
stated that he escaped from Soviet Russia to Harbin in 1930
and was engaged in commerce in that city. In 1931 he arrived
at Shanghai with his family and on September 8, 1931 registered
under No.6769 with the local Bureau of Public Safety as a
Russian emigrant. In Shanghai he owns a factory of neckties
at No.18 Route Delastre in partnership with one Samuil
Grigorievitch Ochakovsky, Russian Jew. It is reported that
Katz is also working as a broker on a commission basis.
I.B. Katz is married to one Ruhma Yakovlevna Katz, Russian
Jewess born in 1890 at Berdichev. They have a son named
Boris born in 1924 at Moschow. Katz is not known to be engaged
in any political activities, and there is nothing against him
in Municipal Police records.

File
2/3
**〔此处转录不清〕**
D. S. Tcheremshansky

D.C. (Special Branch)

主题：荷兰总领事馆关于伊萨克·鲍里斯·卡茨的公函。

由 D.S.切列姆尚斯基（Tcheremshansky）呈报 经由 **〔此处转录不清〕** 转发

根据所附公函进行的查询显示，伊萨克·鲍里斯·卡茨系犹太裔俄国人，1889年7月8日出生于南俄基辅。他称其于1930年从苏维埃俄国逃至哈尔滨，并在该市从事商业活动。1931年，他携家人抵达上海，并于1931年9月8日以俄国移民身份在当地公安局注册，编号6769。在上海，他与另一位犹太裔俄国人萨穆伊尔·格里戈里耶维奇·奥查科夫斯基（Samuil Grigorievitch Ochakovsky）合伙，在德拉司特路（Route Delastre）18号拥有一家领带工厂。据报，卡茨还以收取佣金的方式担任经纪人。
I.B.卡茨娶鲁赫玛·雅科夫列夫娜·卡茨（Ruhma Yakovlevna Katz）为妻，后者系犹太裔俄国人，1890年出生于别尔季切夫（Berdichev）。他们育有一子，名鲍里斯（Boris），1924年出生于莫斯科（Moschow）。卡茨并未被发现参与任何政治活动，警务处档案中亦无对其不利之记录。

存档
2/3

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. ____
Date ____ 18th November 1935.

SHANGHAI, 18th November 1935.

Sir,

I have the honour to inform you that Mr. Isaac Boris
Katz has applied to me for a visa for admission into the
Netherlands Indies.

He is of Russian origin and in possession of a Cer-
tificate of Registration No. 3759, issued by the Bureau of
Public Safety on the 22nd November 1934. He will apply
for a passport within a few days.

According to his statements he was born in Liov, Russia
on the 8th July 1889 and is living at 18 Route Delastre, where
he has a factory of neckties.

He intends to go to Java for about 2/3 weeks to sell
ties, piece goods, caviar etc.

I should be much obliged if you would let me know, if
possible, whether anything is known against Katz from a
political or moral point of view.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,
〔签名〕
Chinese Secretary.

T. P. Givens, Esquire,
Deputy Commissioner (Special Branch),
Shanghai Municipal Police,

SHANGHAI.

§ 2. For report please.
MG
19 Nov 1935

D. S. Tcheremshanovsky.

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Monday, November 18, 1935

Dinner Tomorrow
For Anniversary
In Trade History

Start Of Sino-American
Commerce Recalled
On “Birthday”

CHAMBER, TRADE
COUNCIL MEETING

Speakers Include Kung,
Johnson, Koo And
Julean Arnold

The sesquicentennial anniversary of the opening of Sino-American trade will be celebrated with a banquet by the American Chamber of Commerce of Shanghai and the Chinese-American Trade Council in the American Club tomorrow evening at 8 o'clock.

The program for the event follows:

Presiding hosts: Mr. Cornell S. Franklin, president of the American Chamber of Commerce of Shanghai, and Mr. Chang Kia-ngau, president of the Chinese-American Trade Council.

List Of Speakers

Speakers: Dr. H. H. Kung, Minister of Finance, on "American and China;" Mr. Nelson T. Johnson, American Ambassador to China, on "The Early Decades of Chinese-American Trade;" Dr. V. K. Wellington Koo, Minister to France; and Mr. Julean Arnold, American Commercial Attache, on "Some Aspects of Chinese-American Trade."

Sino-American trade was inaugurated by the sailing ship Empress of China that set sail from New York to Canton on February 22, 1784—George Washington's 52nd birthday—and arrived back in New York on May 10, 1785.

Before Start Of Republic

All this was before the present government of the United States was formed. Only a short time before, the 13 American colonies had organized a semi-nation under the Articles of Confederation and won their independence of England on the battlefields of Bunker Hill and Saratoga and Yorktown.

Robert Morris, financier of the revolt against England, was responsible for the building and dispatching of the vessel to China to enter the China trade. It carried the only product then obtainable in America in which the Chinese were interested—ginseng.

A Famed Drug

To Americans it was but a weed, but to the Chinese then as now, it was an almost universal tonic, often selling for as much as

〔此处转录不清〕

300 to 400 gold dollars an ounce. Originally, it had been obtained exclusively from Manchuria and Korea, but British and Dutch traders had found that the American variety could be sold in China.

Many of the early American trade pioneers conceived the idea of sending a cargo of ginseng on an American ship to Canton, but Morris was the first to put it in practice. Major Samuel Shaw, Bostonian officer of the American Revolution, was placed in charge of the venture as supercargo.

Around The Cape

The Empress of China took the Cape of Good Hope route, the flag of the new and then relatively insignificant country attracting much attention in ports on the way. In Canton it was welcomed by various rival traders, even the English joining in despite the late unpleasantness. Major Shaw was successively dined by each of the 13 nations then represented by ships in the Pearl River, and his voyage was not only the beginning of Sino-American trade, but the first major American venture in world trade.

The net profit of the voyage of the Empress of China was U.S.$30,-000, and in addition to arousing much American interest in China, it resulted in quick development of American exports to this country that soon made American clippers famous all over the seven seas.

纪念
贸易史周年

回顾中美
商业开端
值此“诞辰”

商会、贸易
理事会会议

演讲者包括孔祥熙、
约翰逊、顾维钧和
朱利安·阿诺德

上海美国商会和中美贸易理事会将于明晚8时在美国总会举行宴会，庆祝中美通商一百五十周年。

活动程序如下：

主持东道主：上海美国商会会长康奈尔·S·富兰克林（Cornell S. Franklin）先生，以及中美贸易理事会会长张嘉璈（Chang Kia-ngau）先生。

演讲者名单

演讲者：财政部长孔祥熙博士，题为“美国与中国”；美国驻华大使纳尔逊·T·约翰逊（Nelson T. Johnson）先生，题为“中美贸易的早期几十年”；驻法国公使顾维钧（V. K. Wellington Koo）博士；以及美国商务参赞朱利安·阿诺德（Julean Arnold）先生，题为“中美贸易的某些方面”。

中美通商始于“中国皇后号”帆船，该船于1784年2月22日——乔治·华盛顿52岁诞辰之日——从纽约启航前往广州，并于1785年5月10日返回纽约。

共和国成立之前

这一切都发生在美国现政府成立之前。就在不久前，13个美洲殖民地根据《邦联条例》组建了一个半国家性质的实体，并在邦克山、萨拉托加和约克镇的战场上赢得了脱离英国的独立。

罗伯特·莫里斯（Robert Morris），这位反抗英国革命的金融家，负责建造并派遣船只前往中国开展对华贸易。该船携带了当时美国唯一能引起中国人兴趣的产品——人参。

一种著名药物

对美国人来说，它只是一种杂草，但对当时的中国人而言，正如现在一样，它是一种几乎通用的补药，售价往往高达

〔此处转录不清〕

每盎司300至400金元。最初，人参 exclusively 从满洲和朝鲜获得，但英国和荷兰商人发现美国品种也可以在中国销售。

许多早期的美国贸易先驱想到了用美国船只向广州运送一批人参的想法，但莫里斯是第一个将其付诸实践的人。美国革命时期的波士顿军官塞缪尔·肖（Samuel Shaw）少校被任命为此次冒险活动的货物管理员。

绕过好望角

“中国皇后号”取道好望角航线，这个新兴且当时相对微不足道的国家的旗帜沿途在各港口引起了广泛关注。在广州，它受到了各种 rival 贸易商的欢迎，尽管此前有过不愉快，甚至英国人也加入其中。肖少校相继接受了当时停泊在珠江的13个国家代表的宴请，他的航行不仅是中美贸易的开端，也是美国在世界贸易中的第一次重大尝试。

“中国皇后号”航行的净利润为30,000美元，除了激起美国人对中国的浓厚兴趣外，还促成了美国对该国出口的迅速发展，不久便使美国快剪船闻名于七大洋。

Decem ber 17, 1936.
Afternoon Translation.

The Eastern Daily News ( 東方日報 ) :-

REVOLT OF CHANG HSUEH LIANG

Following the revolt of General Chang
Hsueh Liang, all his former subordinates who used to live
in Shanghai have gone into hiding.
General Chang Hsueh Liang leased the
house at No. 2 Rue Moliere, French Concession, after his
return from abroad. Some say that it was purchased
outright, while others state that it was given him by
somebody as a present. It is a magnificent building located
to the west of the French Park. Opposite is Madame Sun
Yat Sen's house.
General Chang Hsueh Liang used to
have a representative named Tong Kuo Tseng (湯國楨) in
Shanghai, but he went into hiding on December 12 as soon
as he learnt of the Sian revolt. It is said that he was
arrested on December 13; this cannot be confirmed.

China Times and other local newspapers :-

THE VALUE OF LAND : REASSESSMENT DESIRED

Yesterday the local Land Owners
Association sent the following petition to the Shanghai
City Government:-
"The value of land in Shanghai has
dropped considerably during the past year owing to the general
trade depression. Some land owners have gone into bankruptcy.
"The land tax now in force is based
on the value of land as assessed several years ago by the
former Land Assessment Committee of the Bureau of Land
according to the market values at that time. Owing to the
depression and the absence of any prospects for immediate
recovery, most of the land-owners have, at the request of
their tenants, reduced the rent, but they are still paying
the tax according to the old assessed value of the land, and
this has been going on for a long time.
"It is an established law of economics
that the tax should be based on the rent. The present situa-
tion is obviously unfair to the land-owners and several
requests have been received from our members that a petition
be made for a re-assessment of land.
"We hereby request you to order the Land
Bureau to re-assess the value of land with effect from 1937
so that the tax may be reduced."

THE "LIVELIHOOD WEEKLY MAGAZINE"

The "Livelihood Weekly Magazine"
published the following notice in Issue No. 28, Volume 1,
dated December 13:-
"Readers are probably aware that Mr.
Chow Tao Feng (鄒奮), former publisher and editor of the
"Livelihood" (生活), was removed to Soochow on December 4
for detention. On December 6 this magazine received an order
to cease publication, but by virtue of a new registration
made with the Bureau of Social Affairs, the publication of
this magazine will be continued with Mr. King Chung Hwa
(金仲華) as publisher and editor."

《东方日报》：

张学良叛变

继张学良将军叛变后，其所有曾居住在上海的前部下均已躲藏起来。
张学良将军从国外归来后，租赁了法租界莫利爱路（Rue Moliere）2号的房屋。有人说该房屋是直接购买的，也有人说是有某人作为礼物送给他的。这是一座位于法国公园西侧的宏伟建筑。对面是孙逸仙夫人的住宅。
张学良将军在上海曾有一名代表，名叫汤国楨（Tong Kuo Tseng），但他于12月12日得知西安事变后立即躲藏起来。据说他于12月13日被捕；此事无法证实。

《字林西报》及其他本地报纸：

土地价值：希望重新评估

昨日，本地业主协会向上海市政府递交了以下请愿书：
“由于普遍的商业萧条，上海的土地价值在过去一年中大幅下跌。一些地主已经破产。
“目前实行的土地税是基于几年前由前工务局土地估价委员会根据当时的市场价值评估的土地价值。由于萧条且没有立即复苏的前景，大多数地主应租户的要求降低了租金，但他们仍按旧的土地评估价值缴纳税款，这种情况已持续很长时间。
“税收应基于租金是一项既定的经济法则。目前的状况显然对地主不公平，我们已收到多名会员的请求，要求提出请愿，对土地进行重新评估。
“特此请求阁下命令土地局从1937年起重新评估土地价值，以便降低税款。”

《生活周刊》

《生活周刊》在12月13日出版的第一卷第二十八期中发布了以下通知：
“读者可能已知晓，《生活》前出版人兼编辑邹韬奋（Chow Tao Feng）先生已于12月4日被移送苏州拘留。12月6日，本杂志收到停刊令，但凭借在社会局办理的新注册，本杂志将继续出版，由金仲华（King Chung Hwa）先生担任出版人兼编辑。”
